findings.title: Canonical deployment exposes live Claude history on the LAN without authentication
findings.what: The runbook says the container reads live ~/.claude data, exports BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 plus DASHBOARD_ALLOW_INSECURE_BIND=1, leaves DASHBOARD_USER/PASS unset, and calls this unauthenticated posture the canonical LAN deployment. Any peer able to reach the host can read the operator's private dashboard data over plaintext HTTP.
findings.fix: Make loopback the canonical posture. For any beyond-loopback bind, require DASHBOARD_USER and a strong DASHBOARD_PASS (and TLS via a documented reverse proxy); remove the insecure-bind export and describe the guard-disarming LAN mode only as prohibited legacy recovery guidance.
findings.acceptance: The canonical rerun cannot start a beyond-loopback deployment unless authentication is configured; following the documented LAN procedure yields an authentication challenge, unauthenticated requests cannot retrieve dashboard/history endpoints, and the documented URL uses TLS when traffic leaves the host.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read the live-data, credential, canonical rerun, and decision sections at baseline. The document explicitly states that ~/.claude is mounted live, Basic auth is unset, and the guard is bypassed for LAN; this is not an inferred implementation mismatch.

findings.title: Shadow and replay flows lack a fail-closed guard against subscription-OAuth egress of Claude history
findings.what: The guide directs a background subagent to redo the same current task and replay agents to rerun past tasks, then sends results to an LLM judge. It provides consent and spend controls but no content classification, redaction, or exclusion for tasks containing ~/.claude-derived transcript/config content. Because these runs consume the Claude subscription windows, eligible history-derived prompts can be resent using the subscription OAuth credential, violating ADR 0008's absolute invariant.
findings.fix: Add an egress preflight before budget/consent that detects any ~/.claude-derived or secret-bearing task/context and skips it fail-closed. Permit analysis only through the registered, scrubbed, explicit Console-key path; document the skip reason and ensure judges receive only approved redacted fields.
findings.acceptance: A live or replay fixture containing a ~/.claude path, transcript excerpt, OAuth token, or derived history field is rejected before any subagent/judge request; an egress test proves zero subscription-OAuth request bodies contain such content, while a sanitized eligible task still runs.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read the cited flow and baseline ADR 0008. ADR 0008:34-41 forbids subscription-OAuth transmission of ~/.claude-derived content and requires Console key, opt-in, registration, caps, and scrub for permitted analysis; ADR 0008:49-51 explicitly leaves the stricter shadow-calls rule untouched. The audited guide documents budget/consent but no data-egress gate.

findings.title: Efficiency roadmap's dollar and coverage claims are not reproducible from a cited artifact
findings.what: The design bases its North Star, $9,447 monthly bill, 35% coverage, 94% Opus/88% sdk-cli shares, realistic floors, and multi-thousand-dollar lever ranges on a one-time private ~/.claude pull. It names some code symbols but supplies no immutable input artifact, query parameters, field-level provenance, or derivation for the coverage and lever estimates. The pool table arithmetic is internally consistent, but the underlying observations and several recommendation-sized claims cannot be independently reproduced.
findings.fix: Attach or cite an immutable scrubbed accounting artifact and calculation receipt containing the as-of date, exact 31-day bounds, source fields, pricing version/rates, dedup key, formulas, and per-claim inputs. Link each bill/share/coverage/lever claim to its receipt field; otherwise label unsupported ranges as hypotheses rather than verified estimates.
findings.acceptance: A reviewer using only the cited immutable artifact and documented command/formulas reproduces $9,447, each pool share, 94% Opus, 88% sdk-cli, the 35% coverage value, and every retained lever range within declared rounding tolerance; provenance records include source, field, inference, and asOf.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read every numeric section and the verified-code-anchor list, then compared the required auditability contract in docs/adding-a-recommendation.md. Re-derivation confirms 5,449+2,466+1,327+205=9,447, context share rounds to 84%, 9,447/200 rounds to 47x, and the required cut rounds to 98%; the surviving defect is missing reproducible source/provenance for the observations, 35% coverage, and lever ranges—not an arithmetic discrepancy.
